earlier_scan.note: Only wordlists in Glottolog (Roscoe 1915, Condon 1910); no grammar or phonology known.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2018. The autosegmental approach to tone in Lusoga. In D. Brentari & J. Lee (eds.), Shaping phonology, 47-69. Chicago: University of Chicago Press (preprint: UC Berkeley PhonLab Annual Report 2016).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Authoritative account of Lusoga word prosody (every word ends H; no stress contrast); the closest well-described sister (81% lexical similarity) if Kenyi is catalogued under a Soga-Kenyi proxy.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2014. Tonal melodies in the Lulamogi verb. Africana Linguistica 20: 163-180 (see also Hyman & Merrill 2016, Morphology, irregularity and Bantu frication: the case of Lulamogi; Hyman, in press, Prefixal vowel length in Lulamogi, JALL).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lulamogi is reported (Ethnologue 2016) as mutually intelligible with Kenye; Hyman's Lulamogi papers are the nearest first-hand prosodic description (tone: H vs zero, boundary tones) and may comment on Lukenyi; not a Kenyi source but the best proxy.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page keny1278 (Hammarstrom et al.), incl. langdoc full-text queries 'Kenyi', 'Lukenyi', 'Lukenye', 'Lukenhe', 'Bakenyi'
sources.note: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist (Roscoe 1915; Condon 1910); n descriptive refs = 0; all 14 'Kenyi' hits are wordlists, ethnography, history or overviews (Ladefoged et al. 1972; Williamson 1973; Mould 1981; Matovu & Walusimbi 2000).

sources.note: Soga article treats Kenyi as a Lusoga dialect and says only that Lusoga is tonal; nothing on stress; Bakenyi article has no linguistic content.
